speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: An erythematous plaque with areas of crusting, oozing, and irregular borders observed on the dorsal surface of the penile shaft and on the left middle finger. Lesions are firm to touch, non-tender, with no warmth. No palpable cervical, axillary, or inguinal lymphadenopathy. Biopsy findings reveal cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. STD Panel (Syphilis, HIV, HBV, HCV) is Negative.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (SCC) presenting with cutaneous metastasis or synchronous primary lesions.

The presence of a firm, crusted penile plaque with irregular borders and biopsy showing nuclear hyperchromasia and increased mitosis is highly suspicious for malignancy. The concurrent lesion on your finger suggests either a second primary site or metastatic spread, which requires immediate confirmation via imaging of the affected areas. REQUEST IMAGES: Full-body skin map and high-resolution photos of the penile and finger lesions.
